Definition: probably from the same as G736; prompt; Artemis, the name of a Grecian goddess borrowed by the Asiatics for one of their deities:--Diana.
BiblicalUsage: Artemis is the goddess of Ephesus, Diana of the Ephesians, and her silver shrines feed a whole trade. Demetrius the silversmith stirs up the city because Paul's preaching threatens the craft, the crowd fills the theatre crying Great is Diana of the Ephesians, and the townclerk has to calm them, reminding them the city is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Ephesus shows what idolatry really runs on: not only belief, but business. The goddess has silversmiths and a theatre and a city that worships her, and the gospel threatens all of it at once, which is why I hold that the riot is the honest response of a city that knows what it stands to lose.
